items.title: FT008 detour near Gua Musang now open to light traffic after sinkhole
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Oct 25 — A temporary detour at FT008 Section 205.556 along the Gua Musang-Kota Bharu road near the Kesedar Ethnobotanical Recreation Park here was opened to light vehicles at noon today. The detour, which is part of the Central Spine Road (LTU) Project Packages 3B and 3C, is open only to light vehicles. The FT008 federal road near Kesedar Ethnobotanical Recreation Park was closed on Oct 10 following the formation of a sinkhole about eight metres deep.

items.title: Zahid outlines 3 TVET initiatives for rural youth
items.summary: SUNGAI BESAR: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has outlined three technical and vocational education and training (TVET) initiatives to produce skilled workers and entrepreneurs among rural youth. The initiatives are the TVET Premium Career Agreement, TVET Jana Desa and Smart and Green TVET Workshops, which will be implemented in phases. Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister, said the TVET Premium Career Agreement would prioritise early cooperation with employers in selected programmes, including agreements on competencies, placement conditions and salary packages before trainees are recruited.

items.title: Malaysian woman rescued after falling into 10m-deep hole in Vietnam
items.summary: LAM DONG, Vietnam: A 40-year-old Malaysian woman was rescued after falling into a 10m-deep hole while hiking in Da Lat, Lam Dong, on Sunday, the Vietnam News Agency reported. The incident occurred at 5.45am in the Hon Bo mountain area of Lam Vien-Da Lat ward. Hon Bo Mountain, near Thai Phien flower village in Da Lat, is a popular destination for hiking, cloud hunting, and photography, attracting both residents and tourists.

items.title: Takiyuddin: Bersatu invited to PN talks on RoS case, Melaka polls
items.summary: According to News Straits Times (NST), PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said Bersatu leaders had been invited to attend the meeting at PAS headquarters, but whether they would do so was up to them. He said the allocation of the seven seats assigned to PN for the Melaka polls would also be discussed. He said the limited number of seats available meant PN would need to work out a suitable distribution among the parties involved.

items.title: Penang on alert for floods, landslides after fatal tragedy
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang authorities have advised residents to remain alert for flash floods and landslides following overnight rain and high tides. State Infrastructure Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the Malaysian Meteorological Department had forecast rain from Oct 24 to 26. "With continuous heavy rain and high tide levels, flash floods will occur.

items.title: IGP orders immediate CID probe into Noorizwan’s death in custody
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 25 — Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail has directed the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) to conduct an immediate investigation into the death of Noorizwan Zulkefly, who died while in police custody at the Cheras District Police Headquarters (IPD). He said the investigation must be conducted thoroughly following the discovery of several unusual injuries on Noorizwan’s body that warranted further scrutiny. However, police were still awaiting the laboratory report to determine the actual cause of Noorizwan’s death, he added.

items.title: 27 schools in Tebedu to close tomorrow as API exceeds 200
items.summary: KUCHING: A total of 27 schools in Tebedu will be temporarily closed tomorrow after the Air Pollutant Index (API) exceeded 200, with home-based teaching and learning (PdPR) activated. The Sarawak Education Department said the closure involves one secondary school and 26 primary schools, based on ongoing monitoring and API readings recorded at 2pm today. The department said PdPR implementation aligns with the Education Ministry Circular No.

items.title: Takiyuddin: Bersatu leaders invited to PN meeting tonight
items.summary: PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said Bersatu leaders had been invited to the meeting at the Pas headquarters tonight. However, the Pas secretary-general said it was up to Bersatu leaders to decide whether to attend." On the seven seats allocated to PN for the upcoming Melaka polls, Takiyuddin said they would be distributed among the coalition's component parties.

items.title: Malaysian vessel took delivery of 1.16 tonnes of drugs in Andaman Sea
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian vessel intercepted by Indonesian authorities with 1.16 tonnes of ketamine had taken delivery of the drugs from a foreign mothership in the Andaman Sea. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the foreign mothership was believed to be registered in a country within the Golden Triangle region. "Based on information received from the Indonesian National Police (Polri), the drugs were loaded through a ship-to-ship transfer in the Andaman Sea," he told the New Straits Times.

items.title: Melaka state polls: PKR’s 30pc women candidates offer voters a more inclusive choice, says Fadhlina
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL, Oct 25 — PKR’s move to field 30 per cent women candidates in the Melaka state election is part of the party’s strategy to offer voters a more inclusive choice, said Wanita PKR chief Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek. She said fielding more women candidates could also strengthen women’s representation in state politics. Yesterday, PH chairman and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced 21 candidates to contest in the Melaka state election.

items.title: A split second, a lifetime of loss: Family recalls fatal Paya Terubong landslide
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 25 — A 73-year-old doctor was killed when a landslide struck his family's home in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, trapping him beneath collapsed concrete. The victim, identified as Wong Kar Lin, died when a landslide hit the family’s residence at about 8.36am, trapping him beneath rubble in the kitchen while other family members managed to flee. Poh Lim said only the three of them were at home when the landslide occurred, while the couple’s four children live elsewhere.

items.title: Malaysian hiker rescued after falling into 10m-deep hole in Da Lat, Vietnam
items.summary: LAM DONG (Vietnam), Oct 25 — A 40-year-old Malaysian woman was rescued after falling into a 10m-deep hole while hiking in Da Lat, Lam Dong, today, the Vietnam News Agency (VNA) reported, citing local authorities. The incident occurred at around 5.45am in the Hon Bo mountain area of Lam Vien–Da Lat ward, when the woman, identified by her initials G.S.W., was hiking in the area and fell into a hole, said to be part of an abandoned mining site, about 70cm in diameter. Lam Vien–Da Lat ward coordinated with local forces and the Fire Prevention, Firefighting and Rescue Police Division under the provincial Department of Public Security to aid the tourist.

items.title: PH's decades-long bond must endure, says Saifuddin
items.summary: MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan was built on decades of camaraderie that must be upheld by all component parties, candidates and election machinery. PH secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the coalition's strength rested not only on shared political goals but also on mutual trust, respect and loyalty. This is an invaluable political virtue," he said.

items.title: Melaka election: 7 new PKR faces can deliver surprises, says Adam Adli
items.summary: AYER KEROH: PKR has named seven new candidates for the Melaka election to strengthen the party's position in the state. Acting state PKR chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim said the new faces being fielded bring different experiences and responsibilities, offering renewed hope for the party. He said they were "winnable candidates" capable of challenging Barisan Nasional.

items.title: IGP conferred Professor of Practice title
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail was conferred the title of Professor of Practice by Spectrum International University College (SIUC). The title was presented to Khalid by SIUC chairman Tan Sri Professor Emeritus Datuk Dr Mohamed Salleh Mohamed Yasin during the university's 26th convocation at the JW Marriott Hotel Putrajaya. Addressing the 2026 graduating class, Khalid said effective leadership required taking responsibility, making tough choices and prioritising integrity over authority.

items.title: 'Picking up friends' claim no defence for illegal airport drivers
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Drivers caught ferrying passengers illegally at Penang International Airport often claimed they were picking up friends or acquaintances, but this did not deter Road Transport Department (RTD) enforcement action. The department inspected 12 vehicles during an operation that began at 8am, issuing six notices involving three vehicles found carrying passengers without valid permits. From Jan 1 to Oct 24, RTD Penang inspected 1,056 vehicles suspected of operating without valid permits.

items.title: Melaka cafe gig death: Police reclassify case as murder after delivery rider dies; 10 detained
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 25 — Police have reclassified the death of a delivery rider who was seriously injured while attending a gig at a cafe in Kampung Jawa here on October 17 as a murder case under Section 302 of the Penal Code. Melaka Tengah police chief ACP Halim Abas said the case was initially investigated under Section 326 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing grievous hurt using a weapon or dangerous object. “On Oct 17, the victim, a 21-year-old man, was seriously injured while at the cafe to watch a gig.

items.title: Fitch maintains Ukraine at 'CCC', expects war to extend into 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Global credit ratings agency Fitch on Friday maintained Ukraine's long-term foreign-currency rating at "CCC", deep in speculative territory, saying it expects the country's ongoing war with Russia to drag into 2027. The US is pushing to end the 4-1/2-year-old war that has escalated this year as Russia intensified aerial attacks and Ukraine targeted Russia's oil and gas sector. Peace negotiators are meeting next month for new talks Ukraine's sovereign ratings remain in speculative territory as the country relies heavily on foreign financial assistance to fund budget deficits and support the economy while continuing to defend against Russia's invasion Fitch said its rating reflects "substantial" credit risk given the war and its effects, balanced by a manageable near-term debt service profile, an improved level of foreign exchange reserves, and significant support from partners Ukraine is likely to continue running large fiscal deficits due to high wartime spending and weak domestic revenue generation, while its economy is expected to contract marginally in 2026 before returning to growth of 0.2 per cent in 2027, it added Fitch typically does not assign outlooks to sovereigns with a rating of "CCC+" or below © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Protesters clash with police over India's mega-dam project near China
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian protesters angry over a proposed Himalayan mega-dam, intended to counter an upstream Chinese hydropower project, have clashed with police and torched buildings, officials said. The violence in northeastern Arunachal Pradesh state erupted late on Friday during protests against the proposed 11,200-megawatt Siang Upper Multipurpose Project of state-run hydropower company NHPC, Chief Minister Pema Khandu told reporters on Saturday. India says the proposed dam is needed to counter China's US$167-billion Yaxia project, a likely record-breaking hydropower scheme upstream in Tibet.

items.title: Binastra tipped for 21pct earnings growth, gets "Buy" call
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Maybank Investment Bank Bhd (Maybank IB) has initiated coverage on Binastra Corp Bhd with a "Buy" call and a target price of RM3.40. The firm forecasted a three-year forward earnings compound annual growth rate of 21 per cent for the company, assuming annual job wins of RM2.5 billion. Its current outstanding order book stands at RM6.7 billion over 30 ongoing projects nationwide.

items.title: JS-SEZ to drive Johor industrial demand, lift AME Reit prospects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) is bound to be a supportive tailwind for industrial demand in Johor that will benefit AME Real Estate Investment Trust (Reit), said RHB Research. The firm said that it remains positive on AME Reit's prospects supported by the JS-SEZ as well as its resilient portfolio fundamentals, strong tenant retention and embedded rental mark-to-market opportunities. AME Reit's core earnings of RM23.2 million for the first half of financial year 2027 (FY27) accounted for 47 per cent of RHB Research's full-year forecasts and 50 per cent of consensus'.

items.title: Petronas upstream capex rises 19pct, bolstering oil and gas outlook
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's oil and gas sector will be supported by continued upstream investment, offshore activity and recurring contact income amid rising concerns on the renewed Middle East tensions that pushed Brent crude price back above the US$100 per barrel (bbl) level. RHB Research noted that Petroliam Nasional Bhd's (Petronas) capital expenditure (capex) of RM41.4 billion in the first half of 2026 (1H26) looked substantial, but focus should be on the upstream segment. Overall, we believe the growth in upstream investment remains the key positive takeaway for Malaysia's oil and gas sector," it said in a note.

items.title: Warisan seeks 26 seats in next general election, says Shafie
items.summary: SANDAKAN: Warisan is targeting 26 parliamentary seats in the next general election in cooperation with its coalition partners, said party president Datuk Seri Mohd Shafie Apdal. "God willing, we want 26 seats and partner parties to ensure we achieve success and amplify Sabah's voice," he said when officiating the Warisan annual general assembly at Dewan Hakka here today. Also present were Warisan deputy president Datuk Darell Leiking, Parti Kesejahteraan Demokratik Masyarakat (KDM) president Priscella Peter and Parti Solidariti Tanah Airku (Star) acting deputy president Datuk Lawrence Gimbang.

items.title: Cops identify people linked to ketamine tanker, arrests expected
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have identified several people and companies linked to a tanker suspected of involvement in drug trafficking and are working to locate them for arrest, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said. He said illicit activities, including mid-sea transfers, could have taken place. Khalid said Bukit Aman maintained close working relationships with its Asean counterparts, including Indonesia and Laos, as well as international law enforcement partners.

items.title: Philippines probes Thomas Markle laptop over child abuse images as Meghan speaks out
items.summary: MANILA: Philippine police are investigating a laptop found alongside images of child abuse at the former home of Meghan Markle's estranged father, with "full results" expected in a week, the country's interior minister told AFP. "The Philippine National Police (PNP), upon the reports of the son, inspected the former home of a certain Mr. Thomas Markle," Remulla said in a text message sent late Saturday. British tabloid the Sun first reported last week that Markle's son, Thomas Markle Jr., had discovered the child abuse images while going through boxes found in his father's former home.

items.title: MCA to decide in two days if it will still contest Melaka polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MCA will hold an emergency meeting within the next two days to decide whether it will contest the upcoming Melaka election after walking out of Barisan Nasional's candidate unveiling last night. Party president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong said MCA was caught off guard when BN unveiled its candidates after the party had been told that only the coalition's election machinery would be launched yesterday. In 2021, we contested seven seats," Wee told the New Straits Times.

items.title: Fadhlina says RM2,500 allowance for Form Six students to begin in first semester next year
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL, Oct 25 — Form Six students will receive RM2,500 in living allowances starting from the first semester next year, said Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek. She said the allowances, announced under Budget 2027, would be disbursed after the registration process for all Form Six students had been completed. The amount is equivalent to the allowance received by matriculation students and is expected to benefit 90,000 Form Six students nationwide.

items.title: Tropical Storm Champi nears China after battering Taiwan, Japan
items.summary: TAIPEI: A powerful storm swept towards China on Saturday after battering Taiwan and Japan's southernmost islands, knocking out power to thousands of households and forcing the cancellation of hundreds of flights. Typhoon Champi was downgraded to a tropical storm as its wind speed dropped to 102km per hour, according to the latest update from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center. "Although the typhoon is gradually departing, we would like to remind the public that coastal areas will still experience swells and strong wind gusts," the Central Weather Administration's Wuu Woan-hwa said at a briefing.

items.title: 90,000 Form Six students to benefit from RM2,500 allowance from next year
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL: Form Six students will receive a total RM2,500 living allowance from next year, with payments disbursed in stages over three semesters. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the assistance would be channelled during the first semester after student registration was completed. "Once registration for all Form Six students is completed, we will provide the assistance during their first semester.

items.title: Trade Ministry puts the squeeze on uncertified squishy toys, seizes over 5,800 nationwide
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 25 — The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) seized 5,801 squishy toys worth RM70,428 nationwide for failing to display the required Safety Compliance Mark. KPDN Enforcement director-general Datuk Azman Adam said the seizures stemmed from 15 enforcement actions during a Special Inspection on Squishy Toys conducted from October 1 to 14 to ensure compliance with child toy safety standards. “KPDN views child toy safety seriously and will not compromise with any party that fails to comply with regulations under the Consumer Protection Act 1999 (Act 599),” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Wan Rosdy: ECRL to open new doors for east coast entrepreneurs
items.summary: KUANTAN: East coast entrepreneurs must prepare to seize economic opportunities when the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) begins operations in December. National Entrepreneur and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Development Council special adviser Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the ECRL would offer more than just transport connectivity, with the potential to stimulate economic activity, tourism, logistics and trade across Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan. Wan Rosdy said the rail link would open up new opportunities for entrepreneurs to reach more customers, strengthen supply chains and expand their businesses.

items.title: 'I felt my arm swelling': GOF corporal injured in drug suspect's escape bid
items.summary: PASIR MAS: A routine patrol yesterday turned into a frightening encounter for a 41-year-old General Operations Force corporal when a suspected drug syndicate member rammed his vehicle in an attempt to evade arrest. Despite the impact, the corporal and his colleagues immediately got out of their vehicle and approached the suspect's car. However, the incident left the corporal with a fractured right arm, an injury he initially did not realise was serious.

items.title: IGP: CID ordered to probe Noorizwan's death after unusual injuries found
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has been ordered to investigate the death of detainee Noorizwan Zulkefly, 42, at the Cheras police headquarters following the discovery of several unusual injuries on his body. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said police were awaiting the full laboratory report to establish the cause of death. Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim called for a thorough, transparent and uncompromising investigation into Noorizwan's death in police custody.

items.title: UDA unveils show unit for new Residensi Mutiara housing project
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: UDA Holdings Bhd has unveiled a show unit for its latest residential project, Residensi Mutiara, in conjunction with UDA HomeXBites 2026 held here. UDA Land (South) Sdn Bhd chief operating officer Norazim Shukor said the programme gave prospective buyers an opportunity to explore the homes' designs and features, as well as obtain information on unit options, homeownership packages and UDA's property projects in Johor. Norazim said the development, located in the strategic Bandar UDA Utama area, was priced from RM548,700 and featured three bedrooms with either two or four bathrooms.

items.title: Husband to be charged tomorrow with murder of MCBA officer
items.summary: NILAI: A 37-year-old man suspected of murdering his wife, a Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) officer, at the KLIA Quarters on Oct 15 will be charged tomorrow. Nilai police chief Superintendent Johari Yahya said the suspect would face a murder charge under Section 302 of the Penal Code at the Seremban magistrate's court tomorrow morning. "Following instructions to charge, the suspect linked to the death of an MCBA officer earlier this month is expected to be charged tomorrow," he said when contacted today.

items.title: Grandparents, two grandchildren among four killed after Ford hits stranded tow truck on PLUS near Yong Peng
items.summary: Batu Pahat police chief ACP Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani said the 5.50pm incident involved a Ford Ranger, a Toyota Vios and a Scania tow truck. “Muhammad Zaharil Hakimie died while receiving treatment at the Parit Yaani Health Clinic,” he said in a statement today. Shahrulanuar said the accident also left four other occupants of the Ford Ranger with severe head injuries, including its driver, Jumie Julong, 35; his wife, Nor Hakimah Zakiah Ab Shukor, 32; and their son, Muhammad Zafrul Hakimie, 3, who are currently receiving treatment in the Yellow Zone of Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital (HSNI) in Batu Pahat.

items.title: [UPDATED] Perak headmaster transferred amid probe into alleged inappropiate messages to student
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Perak Education Department is investigating allegations that a headmaster of a vernacular school sent inappropriate messages to a female Form Three student. A post on Threads claimed that the headmaster had sent messages, including "I love you", to the student. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said she had directed the state Education Department to investigate the matter.

items.title: PH to contest Melaka polls as one team, says Fadhlina
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL: Pakatan Harapan (PH) will contest the 16th Melaka state election as one team under its 'Melaka Rumah Kita' slogan, said Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek. The PKR Wanita chief said the coalition remained committed to presenting its proposals to voters in the state. The Election Commission has set Oct 31 for nomination day, Nov 10 for early voting and Nov 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka state election.

items.title: SkyWorld deepens Penang push with Batu Kawan expansion
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: SkyWorld Development Bhd is expanding its presence in Penang with the soft opening of SkyWorld Gallery @ Bandar Cassia in Batu Kawan, marking another milestone in the property developer's expansion in the northern region. SkyWorld said the gallery reflects its brand purpose, "Make Living Better", through thoughtfully designed homes that prioritise quality, innovation and improved living experiences. Chief executive officer Lee Chee Seng said the expansion would be supported by innovative construction methods, including prefabricated prefinished volumetric construction (PPVC), to improve building quality and efficiency.

items.title: Billion-ringgit investments alone do not define progress, says Sultan of Selangor
items.summary: KLANG: A state's progress should not be measured solely by billion-ringgit investments, rapid development or high gross domestic product (GDP), but by whether its people benefit from its wealth, said Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah. He said there was little value in a state amassing great wealth if its people continued to struggle. "True progress is achieved when the wealth generated by the state can be enjoyed by all its people.

items.title: Loke announces RM1,000 payout for Melaka taxi drivers ahead of state polls
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 25 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke today said taxi drivers in Melaka will receive RM1,000 in assistance on Monday, with the aid funded through proceeds from the sale of special “H” vehicle registration numbers. Speaking at Pakatan Harapan's (PH) candidate announcement event in Melaka last night, the DAP secretary-general said the assistance formed part of the federal government's efforts to direct public funds towards initiatives that benefit ordinary Malaysians. Loke said the payment would be funded through proceeds from the sale of special “H” vehicle registration numbers, which raised RM91 million.

items.title: Singapore consulate in Kuching to be located within Kuching South City Council area, says mayor
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 25 — The much-anticipated Consulate-General of Singapore in Kuching will be located within the Kuching South City Council’s (MBKS) jurisdiction, according to Kuching South Mayor Datuk Wee Hong Seng. It is noted that the plan to establish a Consulate-General of Singapore in Kuching was first proposed in 2023. During a courtesy call on Abang Johari in January this year, High Commissioner of Singapore to Malaysia Vanu Gopala Menon announced that Singapore intended to set up consulates in both Kuching and Kota Kinabalu to enhance connections in trade, investment and tourism.

items.title: Driver killed after 4WD, car collide in Penampang, police appeal for information
items.summary: PENAMPANG, Oct 25 — A 34-year-old man died following a two-vehicle collision along Jalan Datuk Panglima Banting last night. Acting Penampang police chief ASP Arisanti Aziz said the incident, which occurred at about 8.30pm, involved a four-wheel-drive vehicle and a car. The 34-year-old driver was pronounced dead while receiving treatment at Queen Elizabeth Hospital I in Kota Kinabalu, while the car driver sustained minor injuries.

items.title: Sultan of Selangor: Criticisms aimed at safeguarding people’s well-being, not interfering in govt affairs
items.summary: KLANG, Oct 25 — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, has said that his views, criticisms and concerns on matters relating to the state administration are not intended to interfere in the affairs of the state government. Instead, His Royal Highness said such matters were raised to ensure that the welfare and well-being of the people remained a top priority. His Royal Highness also respects the provisions of the Selangor State Constitution 1959 and the relevant provisions of the Federal Constitution concerning his position and powers as Sultan.

items.title: MBPP halts condo and road projects near fatal Paya Terubong landslide site, orders fresh environmental study
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 25 — The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) has ordered an immediate halt to condominium construction and roadworks on a hillside near the site of a landslide that claimed a man’s life in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, here today. MBPP mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the stop-work order was issued to facilitate further investigations into the incident. Meanwhile, State Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said slope stabilisation works were being carried out in the area, but some sections had yet to be completed when the landslide occurred.

items.title: Court acquits retired Risda employee of six misappropriation charges involving RM15,350 in association funds
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 25 — The Sessions Court here today discharged and acquitted a retired Rubber Industry Smallholders Development Authority (Risda) employee of six charges of misappropriating RM15,350 in association funds about 10 years ago. Judge Azman Mustapha made the decision after finding that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against Mohd Amran Ghazali, 61, at the close of the defence case. Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) deputy public prosecutor Nur Amalina Najwa Mohd Ali appeared for the prosecution, while Mohd Amran was represented by lawyer Muhammad Abdul Rahman Ab Razak.

items.title: Body of doctor pulled from rubble, residents evacuated after Paya Terubong landslide
items.summary: Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations and Firefighting Division assistant director John Sagun Francis said the victim, Wong Kar Lin, 73, a doctor at a clinic, was pronounced dead by Health Ministry personnel. “Firefighters, together with the Civil Defence Force, carried out a rescue operation to extricate the victim, who was buried under the debris, before recovering his body from beneath the concrete rubble. John said the victim’s body was recovered intact, although he had sustained severe injuries.

items.title: Upside-down Jalur Gemilang in Melbourne: Sabah, Sarawak firmly behind Malaysia’s sovereignty, says Mustapha Sakmud
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 25 — The people of Sabah and Sarawak remain firmly committed to upholding Malaysia’s sovereignty and reject any provocation involving the disrespectful display of the Jalur Gemilang by irresponsible parties overseas, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said. He was responding to an incident involving a group of individuals from the ‘Sabah Sarawak Keluar Malaysia (SSKM) Australia’ organisation, who staged a demonstration and displayed the Jalur Gemilang upside down in Melbourne on October 24 in conjunction with United Nations Day. “Disrespecting the symbol of national sovereignty does not reflect the courteous and respectful culture of the people of Sabah and Sarawak,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: One in 23 Malaysian women now face breast cancer risk, up from one in 27, says Nancy Shukri
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 25 — The risk of Malaysian women developing breast cancer has risen to one in 23, compared with one in 27 previously, says Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri. She said that based on the Malaysian National Cancer Registry Report for 2012-2016 and 2017-2021, breast cancer remains the most common cancer among women in the country. She said the programme was later strengthened and rebranded to WeCaRe, which encompasses awareness of breast and cervical cancer among women.

items.title: One dead as landslide hits Paya Terubong house, two escape, says Penang Fire Dept
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 25 — A man was confirmed dead after being buried in a landslide that affected a house in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong here today. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis said it received an emergency call at 8.36am and a team from the Paya Terubong Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene. The operation involved seven firefighters, including a supervisor, as well as a Light Fire Rescue Tender (LFRT) and an Emergency Medical Rescue Service (EMRS) unit, with assistance from the police.

items.title: Sabah Cabinet discusses Tawau water supply disruption amid prolonged dry spell
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 25 — The water supply disruption in Tawau was raised at the Sabah Cabinet meeting last Wednesday to ensure immediate action is taken to help affected residents. “This includes intensifying water deliveries by tanker lorries to affected areas. Nizam said the Tawau Water Department’s latest data showed that operations at the Utara Water Treatment Plant remain affected due to raw water quality problems from Sungai Tawau.

items.title: Zahid: Malaysia reaffirms commitment to assist Indonesia in tackling transboundary haze
items.summary: BAGAN DATUK, Oct 25 — Malaysia remains committed to its offer of assistance to Indonesia to address the transboundary haze affecting the country, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. Ahmad Zahid said the Indonesian government had deployed more than 16,000 personnel along with various aircraft and firefighting helicopters, but aerial operations were facing challenges due to poor visibility. Ahmad Zahid said bilateral communication had already been initiated at the highest level with the Indonesian government leadership to discuss the current situation.

items.title: Even as skies begin to clear, eateries say the haze has already hurt business
items.summary: But at 11.40am, stall owner Che Daud Che Isa had just one customer to attend to. The 59-year-old said business had slowed since the haze began, with some customers choosing to pack their food and eat at home rather than sit down at his stall. “Some customers are also opting for takeaway.

items.title: Anwar congratulates Sultan of Selangor on silver jubilee of reign
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today extended his congratulations to the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee marking 25 years of His Royal Highness’s reign. In a Facebook post, Anwar also prayed that Sultan Sharafuddin would continue to enjoy good health and well-being and continue to lead and protect the people of Selangor with fairness and justice. “Extending my highest congratulations on the occasion of the Silver Jubilee marking 25 years of the reign of His Royal Highness Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah Alhaj Ibni Almarhum Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Alhaj, Sultan and Yang Dipertuan of Selangor Darul Ehsan.

items.title: ‘I have not resigned’: Ismail Lasim dismisses exit rumours, says focus is on Negeri Sembilan Budget 2027
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 25 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has dismissed speculation that he is stepping down, insisting that his full attention remains on preparing the state’s 2027 Budget, which is expected to be tabled at the end of next month. Ismail said the state government was currently concentrating on formulating a budget that would benefit Negeri Sembilan’s more than 1.2 million residents as well as nearly 6,000 state civil servants. “The state government wants 1.2 million residents and nearly 6,000 state civil servants to receive the best benefits and advantages from this budget,” he said.

items.title: Serian top of the haze chart at API 194 as of 10am as 12 areas turn unhealthy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — Twelve areas recorded unhealthy air pollutant index (API) readings as of 10 am today, with Serian in Sarawak recording the highest reading at 194. According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, three other areas in Sarawak also recorded unhealthy readings, namely Kuching (188), Samarahan (182) and Sri Aman (159). A total of 45 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while 11 areas recorded good readings.

items.title: MetMalaysia places Penang and northern states under continuous rain warning until Oct 26
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 25 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) today issued a continuous rain warning at alert level for Perlis and Penang, as well as several districts in Kedah and Perak, with the advisory remaining in force until October 26. Affected areas in Kedah include Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Setar, Pokok Sena, Pendang, Yan, Kuala Muda, Kulim and Bandar Baharu, while the warning in Perak covers Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Bagan Datuk and Hilir Perak. The warning was updated at 9.45am today.

items.title: Overnight downpour floods Penang neighbourhoods, leaving dozens of homes underwater
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Oct 25 — Continuous heavy rain for several hours last night caused flash floods in several areas in Penang, inundating homes in Taman Cantek and Jalan Jelawat here. “The flash floods in Taman Cantek affected 20 houses, with water levels estimated at 0.3 metres (one foot). He said flooding was also reported along Jalan Jelawat in Seberang Jaya as well as nearby residential areas, with water levels estimated at 0.3 metres due to continuous heavy rain and rising water levels in nearby drains.

items.title: Reject politics of hatred and build Malaysia together, Anwar tells Melaka
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged the people of Melaka to reject politics of hatred based on race and religion, and instead strengthen unity as the foundation for national stability and progress. He said this when addressing the candidate announcement and launch of the Melaka PH election machinery for the Melaka state election at the Hang Jebat Stadium grounds here today. Also present were DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke, Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu, PKR vice-president and PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, and Melaka PH chairman Datuk Seri Adly Zahari.

items.title: Malaysia condemns deadly attack on Jordan church, stands in solidarity with victims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — Malaysia has strongly condemned the deliberate attack on the Greek Orthodox Church of St. George in Hamoud village, Karak Governorate in the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan. Wisma Putra said Malaysia reaffirmed its steadfast commitment, together with Jordan, to reject extremism in all its forms and manifestations, regardless of motive or justification. Malaysia also expressed its solidarity with Jordan during this difficult time.
